title: docs: Restructure Git & GitHub 101 into phases
author: adiati98
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #1671

<!--

If you have a pull request related to a current issue please link to that issue number.

That issue can be linked to the pull request by using the side panel in the Github UI or using the `#` symbol followed by the number of the associated issue.

To link a pull request to an issue to show that a fix is in progress and to automatically close the issue when someone merges the pull request, type the keyword "Closes" followed by a reference to the issue. For example, Closes #404 or Closes Virtual-Coffee/virtualcoffee.io/issues/404.

-->

## Description

This PR restructures the Git & GitHub 101 page into four phases. It does not add new content.

- Replaces the heading "Contributing to Open Source with Git and GitHub" with four phase headings. Each phase holds its existing sections:
  - "Setting Up": Forking a Repository, Authenticating with GitHub, Cloning a Repository, Adding an `upstream` Remote Repository
  - "Making a Change": Creating a New Branch, Adding and Committing Changes
  - "Sending Your Change": Pushing Changes, Making a Pull Request
  - "Keeping Your Fork Up to Date": Syncing Your Fork with `upstream`, Synchronizing Changes Locally, Resolving Merge Conflicts
- Moves the sync and merge conflict sections after the pull request.
- Marks "Advanced Git and GitHub Workflows" and "Getting the Most Out of Your GitHub Profile" as optional.
- Updates the sentences that depended on the old order, and links to "Keeping Your Fork Up to Date" from "Making a Pull Request".

<!--

A pull request description describes what constitutes the Pull Request and what changes you have made to the code.

It explains what you've done, including any code changes, configuration changes, migrations included, new APIs introduced, changes made to old APIs, any new workers/crons introduced in the system, copy changes, and so on. You get the gist.

A good description informs everyone that is reaading it of the purpose of the pull request. This helps not just the current maintainers but anyone reading it now or in the future to understand your intent.

If the request is not complete but you want feedback use  Draft Pull Request option of the Pull request dropdown menu.

@mention individuals that you want to review the PR, and mention why. (“ @username I want to know what you think of this code.”)

-->

## Methodology

A good "Why" section should explain the reasoning behind any changes.

title: docs: Update Contributors, Maintainers, and Mentors cards for OSWeave
author: adiati98
body: ## Linked Issue Closes #60 ## Description This PR updates the Contributors, Maintainers, and Mentors cards on the homepage. It removes all Hacktoberfest references and updates the copy to reflect OSWeave: - Contributors card: now reflects that contributors can come from Virtual Coffee or other participating communities and companies, and is inclusive of non-developer contributors. - Maintainers card: now reflects OSWeave's emphasis on being a source of quality, sustainable contributions for maintainers. - Mentors card: now reflects the new ad-hoc mentorship model in Slack, instead of 1:1 mentorship. ### Screenshots ## Methodology ## Code of Conduct > By submitting this pull request, you agree to follow our [Code of Conduct](https://virtualcoffee.io/code-of-conduct/)

title: docs: Update FAQ copy for "What is a Contributor"
author: adiati98
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #80

## Description

This PR updates the FAQ answer for "What is a Contributor and what do I need to get started?" It adds a clear definition of what a contributor is, includes non-code contribution examples (design, writing, community engagement), and removes the old Hacktoberfest-specific text.
